---
title: "code, data & environment versioning"
---

## what should a rerun preserve?

- keep the code revision, input snapshot, reference files, configuration, split rules, and environment
- record seeds and hardware; exact numerical agreement can still depend on libraries, parallelism, and algorithms
- define what counts as agreement: identical files, matching predictions within a tolerance, or comparable evaluation results

## nextflow, docker & slurm

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0"}

| tool | role | record with the run |
|---|---|---|
| nextflow | connect processes and manage task execution | pipeline revision, parameters, nextflow version, reports |
| docker | package software and dependencies in an image | image digest and build inputs |
| slurm | schedule jobs and allocate cluster resources | job ids, requested resources, logs |

:::

- in a bioinformatics workflow, also version the reference genome, annotation, sample sheet, and tool settings
- changing a reference file can change results even when the workflow code is unchanged

## a small nextflow configuration

- this `nextflow.config` fragment belongs beside an existing `main.nf` workflow
- `local_docker` requires docker on the local machine; the `hpc` profile requires access to a slurm cluster and a suitable software environment

```groovy
profiles {
    local_docker {
        process.executor = 'local'
        docker.enabled = true
        // set process.container in your workflow to the required image
    }
    hpc {
        process.executor = 'slurm'
        process.cpus = 2
        process.memory = '4 GB'
        process.time = '1h'
    }
}
```

- nextflow submits tasks through its selected executor; slurm allocates the requested resources [executor guide](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/executor), [slurm guide](https://slurm.schedmd.com/quickstart.html)
- this example does not enable containers for `hpc`; configure the runtime supported by your cluster, such as apptainer, and provide software environments for every process [container options](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/container)

```bash
# with an existing workflow and configured process containers
nextflow run main.nf -profile local_docker -with-report report.html -with-trace trace.tsv
# resume eligible tasks from that run
nextflow run main.nf -profile local_docker -resume
```

- resume needs the task cache and corresponding work outputs; it is a recovery feature, not an independent rerun from scratch [cache and resume](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/cache-and-resume)
- pin container images by digest for an exact image version; tags can change, and image pinning alone does not fix input data or hardware differences [docker image pinning](https://docs.docker.com/build/building/best-practices/)

## check reproducibility

- rerun a small fixed dataset in a fresh output location
- compare outputs or metrics using a tolerance appropriate to the task
- investigate differences in code, inputs, configuration, references, and environment before attributing them to randomness
- keep a compact run manifest linking these records to the [dataset version](../data-pipelines/versioning.qmd)
